messages:
ashok: Heads up — us-west2 onboarding flakiness after we shortened ephemeral credential TTL to 5m (KMS grant change). Several new GPU instances stuck on `fetch-credentials` for ~30s then NodeJoinBackoff. Anyone seeing the same?

maria: seeing it, +1. Logs show repeated 403 from metadata proxy: `grant expired` even though instance started 30s ago.

liam: jumping in — was this the_change we pushed in the auth rollout earlier? I remember a note about reducing grant TTL to reduce blast radius.

ashok: yeah that was the change (auth-rollout yesterday). It improved stale-grant surface but seems to be interacting badly with instance bootstrap retries and our NAT bursts.

liam: suspect path: instance fetches ephemeral cred -> metadata proxy calls KMS with grant -> KMS responds but grant TTL maybe computed from creation time vs issuance -> racing with retry/backoff. Could be clock skew or request ordering.

maria: also noticed audit shipper QPS spiked when these nodes tried to re-fetch -> NAT Gateway had short bursts and started tail-dropping. That caused extra retries and token churn.

ashok: here's a short tail from one affected node: ```
[2026-03-23T18:32:11Z] meta-proxy: GET /token -> 200 -> token exp 00:04:35
[2026-03-23T18:32:42Z] meta-proxy: POST /validate -> 403 (grant expired)
[2026-03-23T18:32:42Z] kubelet: node join failed: credentials invalid
```

sre-oncall: marking this SEV-3 for now. Impact: delayed joins in us-west2, capacity shortfall ~8 GPUs for ~15m. Rolling back TTL quick fix?

liam: short-term rollback possible: restore TTL to previous 1h for grants. That will reduce churn but reintroduce longer-lived grants. We should gate to regions only.

maria: can we instead relax client bootstrap retry to backoff more aggressively (add jitter and cap retries) so NAT bursts don't happen? Might be safer than rolling TTL back globally.

ashok: both are valid. Ops trade-off: longer TTL = less frequent KMS calls but bigger blast radius if a grant leaks. Longer backoff = slower recovery for failed nodes.

liam: propose: 1) immediate mitigate: temp increase TTL to 30m for us-west2 only via feature-flag in auth control plane (no code deploy). 2) medium fix: tune bootstrap backoff + add jitter. 3) long fix: add atomic issuance check so `validate` considers issuance time vs creation time consistently.

maria: +1. I can flip the flag for us-west2 now if we agree. Ops-bot, can you create a rollback change and runbook note?

ops-bot: Created change request CR-2026-033: "us-west2 ephemeral-ttl: 5m->30m (temp)". Approvers: @liam, @ashok. Auto-expire: 6h. Runbook stub attached. :white_check_mark:

liam: approving CR-2026-033. I also updated a quick playbook: check NAT connection metrics -> if NAT tail drops > 1% for 5m, start region flag.

ashok: flipped. Monitoring: nodes rejoining. us-west2 GPU deficit dropping from 8 -> 2 in 3m. Good signal.

maria: opening a postmortem ticket to track root cause and cost implications. Note: increasing TTL will reduce KMS QPS but increase audit footprint lifetime. We should quantify token lifetime effect on audit retention/costs.

liam: cost note: fewer KMS calls immediately reduces our KMS invoice for the hour, but audit + NAT retries caused extra egress/ingest. We'll run a short query against metric-store to estimate 1h delta.

ashok: action items: 
- maria: postmortem + metrics for KMS QPS, NAT drops, node join latency (P0).
- liam: implement bootstrap backoff tweak in next deploy and add jitter (P1).
- sre-oncall: monitor for 1h and ensure CR auto-expires.
- ops-bot: attach runbook and annotate change with links.

sre-oncall: FYI: if we see similar patterns in eu-west, do not flip TTL globally without cross-region checks. We'll coordinate next steps in incident channel.

ashok: thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated if anything flips. :thumbsup:
